problem: Windows takes a very long time to start up
description: The computer takes several minutes to reach the desktop after pressing the power button, and the user has to wait a long time before they can use it normally.
symptoms: Long time on the Windows logo screen
Desktop icons take a while to appear
Hard disk light stays on for a long time after login
Mouse or keyboard is slow to respond right after startup
possible_causes: Too many programs are set to start automatically with Windows
The hard disk is old, full, or failing
Windows updates are installing in the background
The computer has a virus or malware
Not enough RAM (memory) for the installed programs
The disk is a slow traditional hard drive instead of an SSD
Corrupted system files
Too many background services running
diagnostic_questions: How long does it take from power-on to a usable desktop?
Did this start suddenly, or has it always been slow?
Did you install any new software recently?
Is the hard disk light blinking constantly after startup?
How much free space is left on the main drive?
Is this a hard disk (HDD) or solid state drive (SSD)?
Has Windows Update run recently?

commands.purpose: Open System Configuration to check startup settings and services
commands.expected_result: A window opens showing Boot, Services, and Startup tabs
commands.abnormal_result: Window does not open, which may mean system file corruption

commands.purpose: Open Task Manager to see which programs start automatically and how much they slow down startup
commands.expected_result: Task Manager opens with a Startup tab showing a list of programs and their impact rating
commands.abnormal_result: Many programs listed as 'High impact', which explains the slow startup

commands.purpose: Check the main drive for errors and bad sectors
commands.expected_result: Scan completes with no errors found
commands.abnormal_result: Bad sectors or file system errors reported, meaning the disk may be failing

troubleshooting_steps.action: Ask the user how long startup takes and whether it changed recently
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This helps tell the difference between a gradual slowdown (normal wear, too many apps) and a sudden problem (virus, failing disk, bad update)

troubleshooting_steps.action: Open Task Manager and check the Startup tab
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Too many startup programs is one of the most common causes of slow boot times

troubleshooting_steps.action: Disable startup programs that are not needed every day (keep antivirus enabled)
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Reducing the number of programs loading at once speeds up the time to a usable desktop

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check free disk space and delete unnecessary files if the drive is almost full
troubleshooting_steps.reason: A drive with very little free space slows down the whole system, especially on traditional hard drives

troubleshooting_steps.action: Run a full antivirus scan
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Malware often runs hidden processes at startup and slows the computer down

troubleshooting_steps.action: Run chkdsk to check the disk for errors
troubleshooting_steps.reason: A failing or damaged disk can cause very slow read and write speeds during startup

troubleshooting_steps.action: If the computer still uses a traditional hard drive (HDD), consider upgrading to an SSD
troubleshooting_steps.reason: SSDs are many times faster than HDDs and often fix slow startup problems completely

possible_solutions: Disable unnecessary startup programs using Task Manager
Free up disk space by removing temporary files and unused programs
Run a full malware scan and remove any threats found
Repair the disk using chkdsk
Add more RAM if the computer is low on memory
Replace an old hard drive with an SSD
Reset or reinstall Windows if the system files are badly damaged
prevention: Regularly review and limit startup programs
Keep at least 15-20% of the disk free at all times
Run antivirus scans on a regular schedule
Keep Windows and drivers updated
Avoid installing unnecessary software

problem: Linux system fails to boot and drops to a rescue or emergency shell
description: Instead of loading the normal desktop or login screen, the computer shows a black screen with text saying something like 'emergency mode' or 'you are in rescue mode', and asks for a root password to continue.
symptoms: Black screen with white or green text instead of the login screen
Message mentioning 'emergency mode' or 'maintenance mode'
System asks for the root password to fix things
Normal graphical desktop never appears
possible_causes: A required disk or partition failed to mount (for example, listed in /etc/fstab but missing or renamed)
The file system has errors after an unclean shutdown
A recent update broke a system service needed for boot
A full disk with no free space on the root partition
Incorrect changes to system configuration files
A failing or disconnected hard drive
diagnostic_questions: Did anything change recently, such as adding a new drive, editing fstab, or installing updates?
Was the computer shut down properly last time, or did it lose power suddenly?
Can you read the error message on the screen? What does it say exactly?
Do you know the root password to get into the rescue shell?

commands.purpose: View the boot log to find out which service or step failed
commands.expected_result: A list of boot messages showing services starting successfully
commands.abnormal_result: Lines marked 'failed' or 'error' pointing to the specific service causing the problem

commands.purpose: Try to mount all file systems listed in /etc/fstab to see which one fails
commands.expected_result: Command completes with no output, meaning all drives mounted correctly
commands.abnormal_result: An error naming a specific device or mount point that cannot be found or mounted

commands.purpose: Check and repair file system errors on a specific partition (replace sdXN with the real partition name)
commands.expected_result: Scan finds no errors, or repairs minor errors automatically
commands.abnormal_result: Serious errors reported that fsck cannot fix automatically, meaning possible drive failure

commands.purpose: Check how much free space is left on each partition
commands.expected_result: Root partition (/) shows free space available
commands.abnormal_result: Root partition shows 100% used, which can prevent normal boot

troubleshooting_steps.action: Read the on-screen error message carefully and note any file or device names mentioned
troubleshooting_steps.reason: The rescue shell almost always tells you exactly which mount point or service failed

troubleshooting_steps.action: Log in with the root password when prompted
troubleshooting_steps.reason: You need root access to view logs and fix system files

troubleshooting_steps.action: Run journalctl -xb and scroll to find the first 'failed' entry
troubleshooting_steps.reason: The first failure is usually the real cause; later failures are often side effects

troubleshooting_steps.action: If the problem is a missing or bad entry in /etc/fstab, edit the file and comment out or fix the broken line
troubleshooting_steps.reason: A bad fstab entry is one of the most common reasons Linux drops to emergency mode

troubleshooting_steps.action: If the problem is a file system error, run fsck on the affected partition while it is unmounted
troubleshooting_steps.reason: fsck repairs common file system corruption caused by unclean shutdowns

troubleshooting_steps.action: If the root partition is full, delete large unnecessary files or logs to free space
troubleshooting_steps.reason: A completely full root partition can stop essential services from starting

troubleshooting_steps.action: Reboot and confirm the system starts normally
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Confirms the fix worked before considering the issue closed

possible_solutions: Fix or remove the bad line in /etc/fstab
Repair the file system using fsck
Free up space on the root partition
Roll back or reinstall a broken package or driver that broke boot
Restore from backup if the system cannot be repaired
prevention: Always double check /etc/fstab entries before saving changes
Use a UPS (battery backup) to avoid sudden power loss
Keep at least 10% free space on the root partition
Test updates on non-critical systems first when possible
Keep regular backups of important configuration files

problem: Computer shows 'No Internet Access' with Ethernet cable plugged in
description: The network cable is connected between the computer and the router or switch, but the computer cannot browse the internet, and Windows shows a warning icon on the network symbol.
symptoms: Yellow warning triangle on the network icon
Message says 'No internet access' or 'Limited connectivity'
Websites will not load
Other devices on the same network work fine
possible_causes: The Ethernet cable is loose, damaged, or unplugged
The network port on the computer or router is faulty
The computer has an incorrect or missing IP address
The router or modem is not working properly
The network driver is outdated, missing, or corrupted
The network cable is plugged into the wrong port on the router or switch
A firewall or antivirus program is blocking the connection
diagnostic_questions: Is the small light on the network port lit up or blinking?
Does the cable feel loose when you check both ends?
Do other devices connected to the same router have internet?
Has this cable or port worked before, or is this a new setup?
Did you recently install any new software, driver, or antivirus program?

commands.purpose: Check the computer's current IP address, gateway, and DNS settings
commands.expected_result: Shows a valid IP address such as 192.168.x.x with a matching default gateway
commands.abnormal_result: IP address starts with 169.254, which means the computer could not get an address from the router (APIPA address)

commands.purpose: Test if the computer can reach the router (replace with your actual router IP)
commands.expected_result: Replies received with reply times in milliseconds
commands.abnormal_result: Request timed out or destination host unreachable, meaning no connection to the router

commands.purpose: Release the current IP address so a new one can be requested
commands.expected_result: Command completes and shows the adapter with no IP address
commands.abnormal_result: Error message appears, which may mean the network adapter is disabled or broken

commands.purpose: Request a new IP address from the router
commands.expected_result: A valid IP address is assigned
commands.abnormal_result: Still shows a 169.254 address or fails completely, meaning the router or cable is not responding

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check both ends of the Ethernet cable are firmly plugged in
troubleshooting_steps.reason: A loose cable is the single most common cause of this problem

troubleshooting_steps.action: Look at the small lights next to the network port on the computer and the router
troubleshooting_steps.reason: No lights usually means no physical connection, which points to a cable or port problem

troubleshooting_steps.action: Try a different Ethernet cable and a different port on the router or switch
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This helps rule out a damaged cable or a faulty port

troubleshooting_steps.action: Run ipconfig /all and check if the IP address starts with 169.254
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This address means the computer could not get a proper address, pointing to a DHCP or connection problem

troubleshooting_steps.action: Run ipconfig /release then ipconfig /renew
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This forces the computer to request a fresh IP address, which can fix many connection issues

troubleshooting_steps.action: Restart the router and modem by unplugging them for 30 seconds
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This clears temporary problems on the router side

troubleshooting_steps.action: Update or reinstall the network adapter driver from Device Manager
troubleshooting_steps.reason: A corrupted or outdated driver can prevent the network card from working correctly

troubleshooting_steps.action: Temporarily disable the antivirus or firewall to test if it is blocking the connection
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Some security software can wrongly block network access

possible_solutions: Replace a damaged or loose Ethernet cable
Plug into a different port on the router or switch
Renew the IP address using ipconfig /release and /renew
Restart the router and modem
Update or reinstall the network adapter driver
Adjust firewall or antivirus settings blocking the network
prevention: Use good quality, undamaged Ethernet cables
Avoid bending or pinching cables behind furniture
Keep network drivers updated
Restart the router occasionally to clear temporary issues

problem: Wi-Fi keeps disconnecting or dropping randomly
description: The device connects to the Wi-Fi network successfully, but the connection drops every few minutes and then reconnects on its own, interrupting browsing, calls, or downloads.
symptoms: Internet stops working for a few seconds or minutes at a time
Wi-Fi icon shows connected but no internet during the drop
Video calls freeze or disconnect
Reconnecting to Wi-Fi fixes it temporarily
possible_causes: Weak Wi-Fi signal due to distance or walls between device and router
Interference from other wireless devices, microwaves, or neighboring networks
Outdated or faulty Wi-Fi driver
Router overheating or needing a restart
Too many devices connected to the same router
Power saving settings turning off the Wi-Fi adapter
Router firmware that is outdated or buggy
IP address conflict with another device
diagnostic_questions: How far is the device from the router, and are there walls in between?
Does this happen on all devices or just this one?
Does it happen at a specific time of day, or randomly?
Have you recently added new devices to the Wi-Fi network?
Is the router hot to touch or in an enclosed space?
Has the router been restarted recently?

commands.purpose: Continuously ping a stable internet address to see exactly when the connection drops
commands.expected_result: Steady replies with consistent response times
commands.abnormal_result: Repeated 'Request timed out' messages showing the connection is dropping

commands.purpose: Check current Wi-Fi signal strength and connection details
commands.expected_result: Signal strength above 60 percent and a stable connection state
commands.abnormal_result: Signal strength below 30 percent, meaning the device is too far from the router or blocked by walls

commands.purpose: Generate a detailed Wi-Fi history report showing disconnect events
commands.expected_result: Report saved showing few or no disconnect events
commands.abnormal_result: Report shows frequent disconnect and reconnect events, confirming an unstable connection

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check the Wi-Fi signal strength shown on the device
troubleshooting_steps.reason: A weak signal is the most common reason for random disconnects

troubleshooting_steps.action: Move the device closer to the router temporarily to see if the problem stops
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This confirms whether distance or walls are causing the weak signal

troubleshooting_steps.action: Restart the router by unplugging it for 30 seconds, then plugging it back in
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This clears temporary glitches in the router's memory

troubleshooting_steps.action: Go into Wi-Fi adapter power management settings and disable 'Allow the computer to turn off this device to save power'
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Windows sometimes turns off the Wi-Fi adapter briefly to save battery, causing drops

troubleshooting_steps.action: Update the Wi-Fi driver through Device Manager
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Outdated drivers are a common cause of unstable wireless connections

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check how many devices are connected to the router and disconnect unused ones
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Too many connected devices can overload the router and cause drops

troubleshooting_steps.action: Change the Wi-Fi channel in the router settings if neighboring networks are on the same channel
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Wireless interference from nearby networks can cause frequent disconnects

troubleshooting_steps.action: Update the router firmware to the latest version
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Manufacturers release firmware updates that fix stability bugs

possible_solutions: Move closer to the router or add a Wi-Fi extender
Restart the router and modem
Disable Wi-Fi adapter power saving
Update the Wi-Fi driver
Change the Wi-Fi channel to avoid interference
Update router firmware
Reduce the number of connected devices
prevention: Place the router in a central, open location, away from walls and metal objects
Keep router firmware updated
Avoid overloading the network with too many devices
Restart the router periodically

problem: Computer has an IP address starting with 169.254 (APIPA)
description: The computer shows it is connected to the network, but its IP address begins with 169.254, meaning it assigned itself an address because it could not reach a DHCP server, and internet access does not work.
symptoms: No internet access even though the network shows as connected
IP address in ipconfig starts with 169.254
Cannot reach the router or other devices on the network
Problem may affect one device or many at once
possible_causes: The DHCP server (usually the router) is not responding
Physical connection problem (bad cable or Wi-Fi signal)
The router's DHCP service is turned off or has run out of available addresses
Network adapter driver problem
A duplicate IP address conflict on the network
Firewall blocking DHCP traffic
diagnostic_questions: Is this happening on one device or all devices on the network?
Is the device connected by Ethernet cable or Wi-Fi?
Has anyone changed router settings recently?
Does restarting the router or device change anything?

commands.purpose: Confirm the exact IP address and check if DHCP is enabled
commands.expected_result: DHCP Enabled: Yes, with a normal IP address such as 192.168.x.x
commands.abnormal_result: IP Address shows 169.254.x.x, confirming APIPA is in use

commands.purpose: Release the current self-assigned address
commands.expected_result: Adapter shows no IP address after the command
commands.abnormal_result: Error appears stating the operation failed, meaning the adapter itself may have a problem

commands.purpose: Ask the DHCP server (router) for a new valid IP address
commands.expected_result: A new address like 192.168.x.x is assigned
commands.abnormal_result: Still returns a 169.254 address, meaning the DHCP server is still unreachable

commands.purpose: Test basic connectivity to the router
commands.expected_result: Replies received from the router
commands.abnormal_result: Request timed out, meaning there is no physical or network connection to the router

troubleshooting_steps.action: Confirm the exact IP address using ipconfig /all
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This verifies the device really has a 169.254 self-assigned address

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check the physical connection (cable plugged in firmly, or Wi-Fi actually connected)
troubleshooting_steps.reason: A 169.254 address usually means the device could not talk to the router at all

troubleshooting_steps.action: Restart the router
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This resets the DHCP service in case it stopped working

troubleshooting_steps.action: Run ipconfig /release followed by ipconfig /renew
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This forces a fresh request for an IP address after the router restarts

troubleshooting_steps.action: Test another device on the same network
troubleshooting_steps.reason: If other devices also fail, the problem is with the router; if only one device fails, the problem is with that device

troubleshooting_steps.action: If only one device is affected, update or reinstall its network adapter driver
troubleshooting_steps.reason: A broken driver can prevent proper communication with the DHCP server

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check the router's DHCP settings to make sure the address pool is not full and DHCP is turned on
troubleshooting_steps.reason: A full or disabled DHCP pool prevents new devices from getting addresses

possible_solutions: Restart the router to reset DHCP service
Renew the IP address using ipconfig commands
Fix or replace the network cable
Update the network adapter driver
Increase the DHCP address pool size on the router
Manually assign a static IP as a temporary workaround
prevention: Keep router firmware updated
Avoid setting duplicate static IP addresses on the network
Restart the router periodically
Make sure the DHCP pool is large enough for all devices

problem: Websites do not load, but the internet connection itself works
description: The user can browse to some websites by IP address, or apps like games work fine, but typing normal website addresses like www.example.com does not load anything, and the browser shows an error like 'This site can't be reached' or 'DNS server not responding'.
symptoms: Browser error mentions DNS or 'server not found'
Some apps that do not rely on typed website names still work
Pinging an IP address works, but pinging a website name fails
Problem may affect all websites or just some
possible_causes: DNS server is down or not responding
Incorrect DNS settings on the computer or router
ISP (internet provider) DNS server having problems
Local DNS cache is corrupted
Firewall or antivirus blocking DNS traffic
Malware redirecting DNS requests
diagnostic_questions: Can you open any websites at all, or none?
Does the problem happen on all devices in the house, or just one?
Have you changed any network settings recently?
Does using mobile data work fine on the same website (to test if it's the website or your network)?

commands.purpose: Test if the internet connection works using a raw IP address, bypassing DNS
commands.expected_result: Replies received successfully
commands.abnormal_result: Request timed out, meaning the whole internet connection is down, not just DNS

commands.purpose: Test if DNS name resolution is working
commands.expected_result: Replies received, showing DNS successfully translated the name to an IP address
commands.abnormal_result: 'Could not find host' or 'ping request could not find host', confirming a DNS problem

commands.purpose: Clear the local DNS cache which may contain bad or outdated entries
commands.expected_result: Message confirms the DNS cache was successfully flushed
commands.abnormal_result: Error message appears, which is uncommon but may indicate a deeper system issue

commands.purpose: Directly query the DNS server to see if it responds and what server is being used
commands.expected_result: Returns a valid IP address from the DNS server
commands.abnormal_result: 'DNS request timed out' or no response, confirming the DNS server itself is not working

troubleshooting_steps.action: Ping a known IP address like 8.8.8.8 to check if the internet itself is working
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This separates a full internet outage from a DNS-only problem

troubleshooting_steps.action: Ping a website by name, such as www.google.com
troubleshooting_steps.reason: If the IP ping worked but the name ping fails, this confirms DNS is the issue

troubleshooting_steps.action: Flush the DNS cache using ipconfig /flushdns
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This clears any corrupted or outdated cached DNS records

troubleshooting_steps.action: Change the DNS server settings to a public DNS service such as 8.8.8.8 and 8.8.4.4
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This bypasses a potentially broken ISP or router DNS server

troubleshooting_steps.action: Restart the router and modem
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This can fix temporary DNS relay problems on the router

troubleshooting_steps.action: Run a malware scan if the problem is unusual, such as being redirected to strange websites
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Some malware changes DNS settings to redirect users to fake or harmful websites

troubleshooting_steps.action: Test on another device connected to the same network
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This tells you whether the problem is with one device or the whole network

possible_solutions: Change DNS server to a public option like 8.8.8.8 or 1.1.1.1
Flush the local DNS cache
Restart the router and modem
Remove malware that may be hijacking DNS settings
Contact the internet provider if their DNS servers are down
prevention: Use a reliable public DNS server as a backup
Keep antivirus software active and updated
Avoid changing DNS settings unless necessary
Keep router firmware updated

problem: New devices cannot get an IP address from the router
description: When a new device tries to connect to the network, it either fails to connect completely or connects but shows no internet access, while devices already connected continue to work fine.
symptoms: New device cannot join the Wi-Fi or wired network
Existing devices already connected still work normally
New device shows a self-assigned 169.254 address
Router admin page may show 'DHCP pool full' or similar
possible_causes: The DHCP address pool on the router is full (maximum number of devices reached)
DHCP service is turned off on the router
IP address conflict with a manually configured static IP
Router needs a restart
MAC address filtering is blocking the new device
diagnostic_questions: How many devices are normally connected to this network?
Is this a brand new device or one that worked before and stopped?
Does the router have any device limit or parental control settings enabled?
Has anyone set a static IP address on any device recently?

commands.purpose: Check what IP address (if any) the new device received
commands.expected_result: A normal address like 192.168.x.x within the router's range
commands.abnormal_result: No IP address, or a 169.254 self-assigned address, meaning DHCP failed

commands.purpose: View a list of devices the computer has recently communicated with on the network
commands.expected_result: Shows a list of IP and MAC addresses on the local network
commands.abnormal_result: Empty or very short list, suggesting no communication with the router at all

troubleshooting_steps.action: Log into the router's admin page and check the DHCP settings
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This shows the size of the address pool and how many addresses are currently in use

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check if the DHCP address pool is full
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Most home routers only support a limited number of devices by default, often 50 or fewer

troubleshooting_steps.action: Increase the DHCP address pool range if it is full
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This allows more devices to receive an address at the same time

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check for any devices with manually set static IP addresses that might conflict
troubleshooting_steps.reason: A static IP inside the DHCP range can block that address from being given to another device

troubleshooting_steps.action: Restart the router
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This can clear old, unused address leases that are stuck in the system

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check MAC address filtering settings on the router
troubleshooting_steps.reason: If enabled, this feature can block unknown devices from getting an IP address at all

troubleshooting_steps.action: Reduce the DHCP lease time if old devices are holding addresses too long without releasing them
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Shorter lease times free up unused addresses more quickly

possible_solutions: Increase the DHCP address pool size in router settings
Remove or fix conflicting static IP addresses
Restart the router to clear old leases
Disable or correctly configure MAC address filtering
Reduce DHCP lease time to recycle unused addresses faster
prevention: Set the DHCP pool large enough for expected number of devices
Document any static IP addresses used on the network
Periodically restart the router
Review connected device lists regularly

problem: Router is on but no devices can connect to the internet
description: The router's power light is on and Wi-Fi appears to broadcast, but no device connected to it, wired or wireless, can reach the internet, even though local network features (like accessing the router page) may still work.
symptoms: All devices show 'connected' but no internet on any of them
Router lights show power and Wi-Fi, but internet/WAN light is off or red
Cannot open the router's settings page, or can but it shows no connection
Problem affects every device on the network at once
possible_causes: The modem or internet connection from the provider is down
The cable between the modem and router is loose or faulty
The router needs a restart
An outage from the internet service provider (ISP)
Router firmware has crashed or become unstable
Incorrect WAN settings configured on the router
diagnostic_questions: Are all devices affected, or just some?
What color are the lights on the router, especially the internet or WAN light?
Is there a separate modem, and does it show normal lights?
Has the router or modem been moved, unplugged, or affected by a power outage recently?
Have you contacted your internet provider about any known outages?

commands.purpose: Test connection between your computer and the router itself (use your actual router IP)
commands.expected_result: Replies received, confirming the local connection to the router works
commands.abnormal_result: Request timed out, meaning the problem is even before reaching the router

commands.purpose: Test if the router has a working connection to the internet
commands.expected_result: Replies received from the internet
commands.abnormal_result: Request timed out, meaning the router itself has no internet connection, even though the local network is fine

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check the lights on the modem and router, especially the internet/WAN light
troubleshooting_steps.reason: A red or off internet light usually means the connection from the provider is not reaching the router

troubleshooting_steps.action: Restart the modem first, wait one minute, then restart the router
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Restarting in the correct order allows the modem to fully reconnect to the provider before the router tries to use it

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check that all cables between the wall socket, modem, and router are firmly connected
troubleshooting_steps.reason: A loose cable can cause a complete loss of internet even if Wi-Fi still broadcasts

troubleshooting_steps.action: Ping the router's own IP address from a connected computer
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This confirms whether the local network is working, even if the internet itself is down

troubleshooting_steps.action: Ping an external address like 8.8.8.8 from a connected computer
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This tests whether the router can reach the internet at all

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check for an outage by calling the internet service provider or checking with a mobile device on cellular data
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Sometimes the problem is completely outside the home, caused by an ISP outage

troubleshooting_steps.action: Reset the router to factory settings only if other steps fail
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This is a last resort since it clears all custom settings, but can fix serious firmware problems

possible_solutions: Restart the modem and router in the correct order
Reconnect any loose cables
Wait out an ISP outage and confirm with the provider
Update router firmware
Factory reset the router if firmware appears corrupted
Replace a faulty modem or router if hardware has failed
prevention: Use a surge protector to prevent power damage to networking equipment
Restart networking equipment periodically
Keep firmware updated
Keep the router in a ventilated area to avoid overheating

problem: Devices connected to a network switch cannot reach each other or the internet
description: Multiple computers are plugged into a network switch, and either some or all of them cannot access the internet or other devices, even though they were working before or the switch shows power.
symptoms: Some or all ports on the switch show no link light
Devices on the switch cannot ping each other or the router
Switch power light is on but port lights are off
Problem started after adding a new cable or device
possible_causes: The uplink cable from the switch to the router is unplugged or faulty
A faulty port on the switch
A bad cable on one specific device
The switch itself has failed or needs a restart
A network loop caused by connecting two switch ports together with a cable, causing a broadcast storm
VLAN misconfiguration on a managed switch
diagnostic_questions: Are all devices on the switch affected, or just one?
Is there a link light showing on the switch port for the affected device?
Was any new cable or device connected right before the problem started?
Is this a simple unmanaged switch, or a managed switch with VLAN settings?

commands.purpose: Test if a device connected to the switch can reach the router
commands.expected_result: Replies received from the router
commands.abnormal_result: Request timed out, meaning the switch is not passing traffic correctly for that device

commands.purpose: Check if the device connected to the switch received a valid IP address
commands.expected_result: A valid address in the expected range
commands.abnormal_result: No IP address or a 169.254 address, meaning the switch is not passing DHCP traffic

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check the link light on the switch port for the affected device
troubleshooting_steps.reason: No light usually means no physical connection, pointing to a cable or port problem

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check the uplink cable connecting the switch to the router
troubleshooting_steps.reason: If this cable is unplugged or bad, every device on the switch loses internet access, even if local ports look fine

troubleshooting_steps.action: Move the affected device to a different port on the switch
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This helps identify if the problem is a bad port on the switch

troubleshooting_steps.action: Try a different cable for the affected device
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This rules out a damaged cable as the cause

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check if any cable accidentally connects two ports on the same switch (a loop)
troubleshooting_steps.reason: A network loop can cause a broadcast storm that slows down or breaks the entire network

troubleshooting_steps.action: Restart the switch by unplugging power for 30 seconds
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This clears any temporary internal errors on the switch

troubleshooting_steps.action: If it is a managed switch, check VLAN and port settings for misconfiguration
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Incorrect VLAN assignment can isolate a port from the rest of the network even though it appears physically connected

possible_solutions: Replace a faulty cable
Move the device to a working port
Reconnect the uplink cable to the router
Remove any accidental cable loop between switch ports
Restart the switch
Correct VLAN settings on a managed switch
Replace the switch if it has hardware failure
prevention: Label cables clearly to avoid accidental loops
Use quality cables and check them periodically
Keep documentation of VLAN configurations
Use switches with loop protection features when possible

problem: A specific program cannot connect to the internet even though the internet works normally
description: One particular application, such as a game, business software, or printer utility, cannot connect to the internet or a network resource, while web browsers and other programs work fine.
symptoms: One specific app shows a connection error or timeout
Web browsing and other apps work normally
Error messages like 'connection refused' or 'unable to connect to server'
Problem may have started after installing new security software
possible_causes: Windows Firewall is blocking the specific program
Third-party antivirus or security software firewall is blocking it
The program needs a specific port opened that is currently blocked
Router firewall settings are blocking outgoing or incoming traffic
Corporate or network firewall policy blocking the application
diagnostic_questions: Which specific program is having the problem?
Does the exact same problem happen on other computers on the same network?
Did this start right after installing new antivirus or security software?
Does the program need a specific port number to work (check its documentation)?
Is this a home network or a business/office network with a managed firewall?

commands.purpose: Check the current state of Windows Firewall for all network profiles
commands.expected_result: Shows firewall state as ON or OFF for Domain, Private, and Public profiles
commands.abnormal_result: Unexpected settings that do not match what the user expects

commands.purpose: Test if a specific port is open and reachable on a remote server
commands.expected_result: A blank screen or connection confirmation, meaning the port is open
commands.abnormal_result: 'Could not open connection' error, meaning the port is blocked or the server is not listening

troubleshooting_steps.action: Identify exactly which program is affected and what error message it shows
troubleshooting_steps.reason: The exact error often points to whether it is a firewall, port, or server issue

troubleshooting_steps.action: Temporarily disable Windows Firewall to test if the program connects
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This quickly confirms whether Windows Firewall is the cause; remember to turn it back on afterward

troubleshooting_steps.action: If disabling the firewall fixes it, add the specific program as an allowed app in Windows Firewall settings instead of leaving the firewall off
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This keeps the computer protected while allowing the needed program to work

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check third-party antivirus software for its own separate firewall settings
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Many antivirus programs have their own firewall that works independently from Windows Firewall

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check if the program needs specific ports opened, and confirm those ports are allowed in both the computer firewall and the router
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Some programs, especially games and remote access tools, require specific ports to function properly

troubleshooting_steps.action: Test the same program on another computer on the same network
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This helps determine if the problem is specific to one computer or affects the whole network

troubleshooting_steps.action: On business networks, check with the network administrator about firewall policies
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Company firewalls often block certain apps or ports by policy, which a regular user cannot change

possible_solutions: Add the program as an allowed app in Windows Firewall
Adjust third-party antivirus firewall settings
Open the required port in the firewall and router settings
Request an exception from a corporate network administrator
Reinstall the program if its firewall rule became corrupted
prevention: Review firewall rules when installing new network-dependent software
Keep a record of which ports specific applications need
Avoid running two firewall or antivirus programs at the same time
Test new software on a single machine before wide deployment on business networks

problem: Printer shows offline even though it is turned on
description: The printer is powered on and appears ready, but the computer shows the printer as 'offline' in the printer list, and print jobs will not print or get stuck.
symptoms: Printer icon shows 'offline' status on the computer
Print jobs stay stuck in the print queue
Printer's own screen shows it is ready and has paper and ink
Problem may affect one computer or all computers trying to print
possible_causes: The printer lost its network or USB connection
The printer's IP address changed (common with network printers)
The print spooler service on the computer has stopped or is stuck
The printer is set to 'Use Printer Offline' mode by mistake
The printer is out of paper, ink, or has a paper jam, and Windows misreports this as offline
Wi-Fi connection to the printer dropped
diagnostic_questions: Is this a USB printer, network printer, or wireless printer?
Does the printer's own screen show any errors, like paper jam or low ink?
Is this happening on one computer, or all computers that try to print?
Has the printer or router been restarted recently, or the network changed?

commands.purpose: Test if the computer can reach the network printer
commands.expected_result: Replies received from the printer
commands.abnormal_result: Request timed out, meaning the printer's IP address may have changed or the printer lost network connection

commands.purpose: Open the Services window to check the status of the Print Spooler service
commands.expected_result: Print Spooler service status shows 'Running'
commands.abnormal_result: Service is stopped, which prevents any printing from working

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check the printer's own screen for any error messages, such as paper jam or out of ink
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Physical printer errors can cause it to show as offline even though it is powered on

troubleshooting_steps.action: Confirm the printer is properly connected, either by USB cable or to the Wi-Fi network
troubleshooting_steps.reason: A dropped connection is one of the most common causes of the offline status

troubleshooting_steps.action: Go to printer settings on the computer and make sure 'Use Printer Offline' is not accidentally turned on
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Windows sometimes gets stuck in this mode after a temporary disconnection

troubleshooting_steps.action: For network printers, ping the printer's IP address to confirm it is reachable
troubleshooting_steps.reason: If the printer's IP address changed, the computer may still be trying to reach the old address

troubleshooting_steps.action: Restart the Print Spooler service using services.msc
troubleshooting_steps.reason: A stuck print spooler service is a common software cause of printers showing offline

troubleshooting_steps.action: Remove the printer from the computer and add it again
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This refreshes the connection details and often fixes an outdated IP address or driver issue

troubleshooting_steps.action: Restart both the printer and the computer
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This clears temporary glitches on both the printer and the computer's printing system

possible_solutions: Turn off 'Use Printer Offline' mode in printer settings
Restart the Print Spooler service
Reconnect the printer to Wi-Fi or check the USB cable
Update the printer's IP address on the computer, or set a static IP on the printer
Remove and re-add the printer
Update or reinstall the printer driver
prevention: Set network printers to use a fixed (static) IP address
Keep printer firmware and drivers updated
Avoid moving the printer far from the Wi-Fi router
Regularly check for paper jams and low ink or toner

problem: Cannot access a shared folder on another computer
description: The user tries to open a shared folder on another computer over the network, but gets an error message such as 'Access is denied', 'Network path was not found', or the folder simply does not appear.
symptoms: Error message 'Access is denied' when opening the shared folder
Error message 'The network path was not found'
Shared folder does not appear when browsing the network
Problem may affect one user or several
possible_causes: File and printer sharing is turned off on the host computer
The user does not have permission to access the shared folder
The host computer is turned off, sleeping, or disconnected from the network
A firewall is blocking file sharing traffic
Incorrect username or password entered for the shared computer
Network discovery is turned off
diagnostic_questions: Is the computer that owns the shared folder turned on and connected to the network?
Do you know the exact folder path, such as \\ComputerName\FolderName?
Does this happen for everyone trying to access the folder, or just you?
Have you successfully accessed this shared folder before?
What exact error message appears?

commands.purpose: Check if the computer sharing the folder is reachable on the network
commands.expected_result: Replies received from the host computer
commands.abnormal_result: Request timed out, meaning the host computer is off, asleep, or disconnected

commands.purpose: Attempt to connect to the shared folder directly and see any detailed error
commands.expected_result: Command completes successfully, confirming the connection
commands.abnormal_result: Error such as 'System error 5 has occurred. Access is denied', pointing to a permissions problem

commands.purpose: List all shared folders available on a specific computer
commands.expected_result: Shows a list of shared folder names
commands.abnormal_result: Error message, meaning either the computer is unreachable or sharing is disabled

troubleshooting_steps.action: Confirm the host computer is turned on, awake, and connected to the same network
troubleshooting_steps.reason: A shared folder is only available while the hosting computer is running and reachable

troubleshooting_steps.action: Ping the host computer's name or IP address from the computer having trouble
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This confirms basic network connectivity before checking sharing settings

troubleshooting_steps.action: On the host computer, confirm that file and printer sharing is turned on in Network settings
troubleshooting_steps.reason: If sharing is disabled, no other computer can access folders on it, no matter how they connect

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check the specific folder's sharing permissions and make sure the correct user or 'Everyone' has access
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Even with sharing enabled overall, a specific folder may not be shared with the right person

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check both computers' firewall settings allow 'File and Printer Sharing'
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Firewalls often block this type of traffic by default for security

troubleshooting_steps.action: Try accessing the folder using its IP address instead of computer name
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This helps identify if the problem is with name resolution rather than the sharing itself

troubleshooting_steps.action: Enable Network Discovery on both computers
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Without this setting, computers may not be able to see or browse each other on the network

possible_solutions: Turn on file and printer sharing on the host computer
Grant the correct permissions to the shared folder
Allow file sharing traffic through the firewall on both computers
Enable network discovery
Use the correct username and password when prompted
Access the share using its IP address if name resolution fails
prevention: Document shared folder permissions for future reference
Keep host computers awake or set proper wake settings if shares are needed regularly
Standardize firewall rules for sharing across office computers
Use a dedicated file server for frequently accessed shares

problem: User cannot log in to a domain-joined computer
description: An employee tries to log in to their work computer using their normal username and password, but gets an error saying the login failed, even though they are sure the password is correct.
symptoms: Error message such as 'The trust relationship between this workstation and the primary domain failed'
Error message 'The username or password is incorrect'
Login screen shows 'domain not available' or similar
Other users on the same computer or network may or may not have the same problem
possible_causes: The user typed the wrong password, or Caps Lock is on
The account is locked out after too many failed attempts
The computer lost its trust relationship with the domain controller (common after reinstalling Windows or restoring an old backup)
The domain controller server is unreachable or down
The computer's network connection is not working
The user's account has expired or been disabled by an administrator
Time difference between the computer and the domain controller is too large
diagnostic_questions: What is the exact error message shown on the login screen?
Has this account worked before on this specific computer?
Can the user log in on a different computer with the same account?
Was the computer recently reimaged, reinstalled, or restored from an old backup?
Is the computer connected to the network right now?

commands.purpose: Check if the computer can reach the domain controller server
commands.expected_result: Replies received from the domain controller
commands.abnormal_result: Request timed out, meaning the computer cannot reach the domain controller, likely a network problem

commands.purpose: Check the secure channel (trust relationship) status between the computer and the domain
commands.expected_result: Message shows the trust test completed successfully
commands.abnormal_result: Message shows a failure, confirming a broken trust relationship that needs to be repaired

commands.purpose: Check if the computer's clock is properly synced, since large time differences can block domain login
commands.expected_result: Shows a recent, successful time sync
commands.abnormal_result: Shows sync errors or a large time offset, which can cause authentication failures

troubleshooting_steps.action: Confirm the exact error message shown on screen
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Different error messages point to very different causes, such as wrong password versus broken trust relationship

troubleshooting_steps.action: Try logging in with a different, known-working domain account on the same computer
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This helps determine if the problem is with the user's account or the computer itself

troubleshooting_steps.action: Confirm the computer has a working network connection to reach the domain controller
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Without network access, the computer cannot verify domain login credentials

troubleshooting_steps.action: If the error mentions 'trust relationship failed', this usually means the computer needs to be removed and re-added to the domain
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This error means the computer's security credentials no longer match what the domain controller has on record

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check with an administrator if the user's account might be locked, disabled, or expired
troubleshooting_steps.reason: These account-level issues can only be fixed by someone with administrator access to Active Directory

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check the computer's date and time settings match the correct time zone and are accurate
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Domain authentication can fail if the computer's clock is too far off from the domain controller's clock

troubleshooting_steps.action: If all else fails and the trust relationship is broken, log in with a local administrator account, disjoin and rejoin the computer to the domain, then restart
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This resets the security relationship between the computer and the domain, resolving trust errors

possible_solutions: Reset the user's password if it was simply incorrect or expired
Unlock the account through an administrator if it was locked out
Fix network connectivity issues preventing contact with the domain controller
Rejoin the computer to the domain to repair a broken trust relationship
Correct the computer's date, time, and time zone settings
prevention: Avoid restoring very old backups of domain-joined computers
Keep computer clocks synced automatically
Set reasonable account lockout policies to avoid frequent lockouts
Document domain rejoin procedures for IT staff

problem: Microsoft Word, Excel, or another Office program will not open or crashes immediately
description: When the user tries to open a Microsoft Office application like Word or Excel, the program either does not open at all, shows an error message, or opens briefly and then closes by itself.
symptoms: Program window flashes briefly and then disappears
Error message about the program 'has stopped working'
Program hangs on a loading screen and never fully opens
Other Office programs may or may not have the same problem
possible_causes: A corrupted Office program file or installation
A problematic add-in is causing the crash
Windows needs important updates
The Office license or activation has a problem
A corrupted user settings/profile for Office
Conflicting antivirus software
Not enough free disk space or memory
diagnostic_questions: Does this happen with just one Office program, or all of them (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, etc.)?
Did this start after a recent update or new add-in installation?
Does the program open in Safe Mode?
Is there any specific error message or error code shown?
Does this happen with every document, or a specific file?

commands.purpose: Open Word in Safe Mode, which disables add-ins, to see if the program opens without them
commands.expected_result: Word opens successfully in Safe Mode
commands.abnormal_result: Word still crashes even in Safe Mode, suggesting a deeper installation problem rather than an add-in

commands.purpose: Scan and repair corrupted Windows system files that could be affecting Office
commands.expected_result: Scan completes and reports no integrity violations, or successfully repairs found issues
commands.abnormal_result: Scan reports it found corrupt files but could not fix them, requiring further repair steps

troubleshooting_steps.action: Try opening a different Office program, such as Excel instead of Word
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This tells you if the problem is with one specific program or the whole Office installation

troubleshooting_steps.action: Try opening the program in Safe Mode by holding Ctrl while opening it, or typing winword /safe in the Run box
troubleshooting_steps.reason: If it opens fine in Safe Mode, a problematic add-in is likely the cause

troubleshooting_steps.action: If Safe Mode works, go to File > Options > Add-ins and disable recently added add-ins
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This isolates and removes the specific add-in causing the crash

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check for and install any pending Windows updates
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Sometimes Office compatibility problems are fixed by installing the latest Windows updates

troubleshooting_steps.action: Use the built-in Office repair tool (Control Panel > Programs > Microsoft Office > Change > Quick Repair)
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This automatically fixes many common causes of Office crashes without needing to reinstall everything

troubleshooting_steps.action: If Quick Repair does not work, try the Online Repair option, which reinstalls Office components
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Online Repair fixes deeper corruption that Quick Repair cannot resolve

troubleshooting_steps.action: Create a new Windows user profile and test if Office opens normally under that profile
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This checks if the problem is caused by a corrupted user profile rather than Office itself

troubleshooting_steps.action: As a last resort, uninstall and reinstall Office completely
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This replaces all Office files fresh, fixing almost any software-level corruption

possible_solutions: Disable a problematic add-in
Run Office Quick Repair or Online Repair
Install pending Windows updates
Create a new Windows user profile to test
Reinstall Microsoft Office completely
Check Office activation status and re-activate if needed
prevention: Only install trusted, necessary Office add-ins
Keep Windows and Office updated regularly
Avoid forcefully closing Office programs, which can corrupt settings
Keep enough free disk space for Office to function properly

problem: A device shows a warning icon in Device Manager and does not work properly
description: A hardware device, such as a graphics card, network adapter, or sound card, is not working correctly, and when checked in Device Manager, it shows a yellow warning triangle or similar error symbol.
symptoms: Yellow warning triangle next to a device name in Device Manager
The device (like sound, graphics, or network) is not working
Error message such as 'This device cannot start (Code 10)'
Device may appear as 'Unknown Device'
possible_causes: The driver for the device is missing, outdated, or corrupted
A recent Windows update replaced the driver with an incompatible one
Hardware conflict with another device
Physical hardware failure
The driver was not properly installed after a fresh Windows install
Corrupted system files affecting driver loading
diagnostic_questions: Which specific device is showing the error (graphics, sound, network, etc.)?
What error code appears if you double-click the device and check its properties?
Did this start after a Windows update or after installing new hardware?
Has this device ever worked correctly on this computer?

commands.purpose: Open Device Manager to view all hardware devices and their status
commands.expected_result: All devices show as working normally, with no warning icons
commands.abnormal_result: Device shows a yellow warning triangle, red X, or question mark icon, indicating a problem

commands.purpose: Repair corrupted Windows system files that might affect driver loading
commands.expected_result: No integrity violations found, or successful repair of found issues
commands.abnormal_result: Corrupt files found that cannot be repaired automatically

troubleshooting_steps.action: Open Device Manager and find the device showing the warning icon
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This confirms exactly which device has the problem and what error code it shows

troubleshooting_steps.action: Right-click the device and choose 'Update driver' to search automatically for updated software
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This can fix problems caused by an outdated or slightly corrupted driver

troubleshooting_steps.action: If updating does not work, right-click and choose 'Uninstall device', then restart the computer
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Windows will often reinstall a fresh, working version of the driver automatically on restart

troubleshooting_steps.action: Download the latest driver directly from the hardware manufacturer's website using another working computer if needed, and install it manually
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Manufacturer drivers are often more up to date and reliable than the ones Windows finds automatically

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check if this problem started right after a Windows update, and if so, try rolling back the driver to the previous version
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Some Windows updates install drivers that are not fully compatible with certain hardware

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check for hardware conflicts by looking at the device's resource settings in Device Manager properties
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Rarely, two devices can conflict over the same system resources, causing one to fail

troubleshooting_steps.action: If the device still fails after driver reinstall, test the hardware in another computer if possible
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This helps determine if the problem is the driver/software or the physical hardware itself

possible_solutions: Update the driver through Device Manager
Uninstall and let Windows reinstall the driver automatically
Download and install the latest driver from the manufacturer's website
Roll back to a previous driver version
Replace faulty hardware if the device fails on another computer too
prevention: Keep drivers updated through the manufacturer's official website
Create a system restore point before major driver updates
Avoid installing drivers from untrusted third-party websites
Check hardware compatibility before major Windows updates

problem: Computer turns on but does not display anything on the screen
description: When the power button is pressed, the computer's fans spin and lights turn on, but the monitor stays black and shows no picture at all, not even the manufacturer's logo.
symptoms: Computer fans and lights turn on normally
Monitor shows 'No signal' or stays completely black
No beep sounds, or a pattern of beep sounds is heard
Keyboard lights (Caps Lock, Num Lock) may or may not respond
possible_causes: The monitor cable is loose or connected to the wrong port
The monitor itself is turned off or set to the wrong input source
A loose or failing RAM (memory) stick
A failing graphics card
A loose power connection inside the computer
A failed motherboard component
The computer is not actually powering on, only the fans spinning while other parts fail
diagnostic_questions: Are the computer's fans spinning and lights on?
Is the monitor itself turned on, and is it set to the correct input source (HDMI, DisplayPort, etc.)?
Do you hear any beep sounds when the computer starts?
Was anything opened inside the computer recently, such as adding memory or cleaning dust?
Does this happen every time, or only sometimes?

troubleshooting_steps.action: Confirm the monitor itself is turned on and set to the correct input source
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This is a very common and simple cause that is often overlooked

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check that the video cable is firmly connected at both the computer and monitor ends
troubleshooting_steps.reason: A loose or wrong cable connection prevents any picture from displaying

troubleshooting_steps.action: Try a different video cable or a different port on the computer if available (such as switching from HDMI to DisplayPort)
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This helps rule out a damaged cable or faulty port

troubleshooting_steps.action: Test the monitor on another computer, or test another monitor on this computer
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This confirms whether the problem is with the monitor or the computer itself

troubleshooting_steps.action: Listen carefully for beep sounds during startup and note the pattern
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Different beep patterns indicate different hardware problems, such as memory or graphics card issues

troubleshooting_steps.action: If comfortable opening the computer case, check that the RAM sticks and graphics card are firmly seated in their slots
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Loose internal components are a common cause of a computer that powers on but shows no display

troubleshooting_steps.action: If there is more than one RAM stick, try starting the computer with only one stick installed at a time
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This helps identify if a single faulty memory stick is preventing the computer from displaying anything

troubleshooting_steps.action: If the computer has a separate graphics card, try connecting the monitor directly to the motherboard's video port instead
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This helps determine if a failing graphics card is the cause of the no-display problem

possible_solutions: Turn on the monitor or select the correct input source
Reconnect or replace the video cable
Reseat RAM sticks and the graphics card
Test with a single RAM stick to find a faulty one
Test using the motherboard's built-in video port instead of a graphics card
Replace failed hardware components such as RAM or graphics card
prevention: Handle internal components carefully to avoid loosening connections
Keep the inside of the computer free from dust buildup
Avoid moving the computer while it is powered on
Use a surge protector to prevent power-related hardware damage

problem: Computer shows a blue screen error and restarts unexpectedly
description: While using the computer normally, the screen suddenly turns blue with white text showing an error code and message, then the computer restarts on its own, sometimes losing unsaved work.
symptoms: Sudden blue screen with white error text
Computer restarts automatically after the blue screen
Error code shown, such as 'MEMORY_MANAGEMENT' or 'IRQL_NOT_LESS_OR_EQUAL'
May happen randomly or only during specific activities like gaming or printing
possible_causes: A faulty or incompatible driver
Failing or faulty RAM (memory)
Overheating hardware components
Corrupted Windows system files
A failing hard disk or SSD
Incompatible or corrupted software
Power supply providing unstable power to components
diagnostic_questions: What is the exact error code or message shown on the blue screen (if you can note it before it restarts)?
Does this happen randomly, or during a specific activity like gaming, printing, or opening a certain program?
Did this start after installing new hardware, drivers, or software?
How often does this happen, once a week, once a day, or several times a day?
Is the computer feeling unusually hot when this happens?

commands.purpose: Check if the computer is set to automatically restart after a blue screen, which can be disabled to allow reading the error message
commands.expected_result: Shows current setting for auto reboot
commands.abnormal_result: Not applicable, this is just informational

commands.purpose: Open Windows Memory Diagnostic tool to test RAM for errors
commands.expected_result: Tool completes and reports no memory problems found
commands.abnormal_result: Tool reports memory errors, confirming faulty RAM as a likely cause

commands.purpose: Scan and repair corrupted Windows system files that could cause crashes
commands.expected_result: No integrity violations found, or issues successfully repaired
commands.abnormal_result: Corrupt files found that could not be repaired, requiring further steps like DISM or reinstall

commands.purpose: Check the main drive for file system errors or bad sectors that could cause crashes
commands.expected_result: No errors found on the disk
commands.abnormal_result: Errors or bad sectors found, suggesting the disk may be failing

troubleshooting_steps.action: Write down the exact error code shown on the blue screen the next time it happens
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Different error codes point to very different causes, such as memory problems versus driver problems

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check the Reliability Monitor or Event Viewer for details about what happened right before the crash
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Windows logs details that can point to the exact driver or program involved in the crash

troubleshooting_steps.action: If the crashes started after installing new hardware or a driver, try removing or rolling back that driver
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Incompatible drivers are one of the most common causes of blue screen crashes

troubleshooting_steps.action: Run the Windows Memory Diagnostic tool to test for faulty RAM
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Faulty memory is a very common hardware cause of random blue screens

troubleshooting_steps.action: Run sfc /scannow to check for and repair corrupted system files
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Corrupted system files can cause instability leading to crashes

troubleshooting_steps.action: Run chkdsk to check the hard drive or SSD for errors
troubleshooting_steps.reason: A failing storage drive can cause system files to become corrupted, leading to crashes

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check if the computer is overheating using built-in temperature monitoring tools or checking if fans and vents are clogged with dust
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Overheating can cause the system to crash suddenly to protect the hardware

troubleshooting_steps.action: Update all drivers, especially graphics and chipset drivers, to their latest stable versions
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Keeping drivers current fixes many known stability bugs

troubleshooting_steps.action: As a last resort, consider a clean reinstall of Windows if the cause cannot be found
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This removes any deep software corruption that could not be fixed through repair tools

possible_solutions: Roll back or update the driver causing the crash
Replace faulty RAM found during memory diagnostics
Repair corrupted system files using sfc /scannow
Fix disk errors using chkdsk
Clean dust from the computer to fix overheating
Reinstall Windows if the problem cannot be resolved otherwise
prevention: Keep drivers updated from official manufacturer sources
Regularly clean dust from the computer to prevent overheating
Avoid installing software from untrusted sources
Perform regular disk checks and system file scans

problem: Computer is generally slow when opening programs and switching between windows
description: The computer takes a noticeably long time to open programs, switch between open windows, or respond to clicks, even though it used to work faster before.
symptoms: Programs take a long time to open
Switching between windows feels delayed
Mouse cursor sometimes shows a spinning circle for several seconds
The computer becomes very slow, especially with several programs open at once
possible_causes: Too many programs running in the background
Not enough RAM (memory) for current usage
Hard disk nearly full or old and slow
Malware or virus running hidden processes
Too many browser tabs or extensions open
Overheating causing the processor to slow itself down
Outdated hardware no longer able to keep up with current software
diagnostic_questions: Did this slowness happen gradually over time, or did it start suddenly?
How much RAM does the computer have, and how many programs are usually open at once?
How much free space is left on the main drive?
Have you noticed any strange pop-ups or unfamiliar programs recently?
Does the computer feel hot or does the fan run loudly during normal use?

commands.purpose: Open Task Manager to check CPU, memory, and disk usage in real time
commands.expected_result: Usage percentages stay reasonable, generally under 80-90% during normal tasks
commands.abnormal_result: CPU, memory, or disk usage stuck near 100% even when idle, pointing to a specific problem process

commands.purpose: Open Disk Cleanup to remove temporary files and free up space
commands.expected_result: Tool shows space that can be freed, and cleans it after confirmation
commands.abnormal_result: Very little space can be freed, meaning the disk is genuinely full of needed files or programs

troubleshooting_steps.action: Open Task Manager and check the Processes tab, sorting by CPU and then by Memory usage
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This quickly identifies which program or process is using the most resources and slowing the system down

troubleshooting_steps.action: Close unnecessary programs and browser tabs that are not being used
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Each open program uses memory and processing power, and closing unused ones frees up resources immediately

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check the Startup tab in Task Manager and disable unnecessary startup programs
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Fewer background programs running means more resources available for the programs you actually want to use

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check available disk space and free up space if the drive is nearly full
troubleshooting_steps.reason: A nearly full drive, especially an older hard disk, slows down the entire computer significantly

troubleshooting_steps.action: Run a full antivirus and malware scan
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Hidden malicious programs often use significant system resources without the user's knowledge

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check how many browser tabs and extensions are open, and close or remove ones not needed
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Web browsers with many tabs and extensions can use a large amount of memory

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check if the computer is overheating by monitoring temperatures or listening for unusually loud fan noise
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Modern processors slow themselves down automatically to prevent damage when they get too hot

troubleshooting_steps.action: Consider upgrading RAM or switching to an SSD if the computer is old and the hardware is simply outdated
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Sometimes the hardware itself can no longer keep up with current software demands, and an upgrade is the most effective fix

possible_solutions: Close unnecessary background programs and browser tabs
Disable unneeded startup programs
Free up disk space
Remove malware found during a scan
Clean dust from the computer to fix overheating
Upgrade RAM or switch from a hard disk to an SSD
prevention: Regularly restart the computer instead of leaving it on for weeks
Keep the number of startup programs to a minimum
Perform regular malware scans
Keep at least 15-20% of the disk free
Clean dust from vents and fans periodically

problem: Computer shows strange pop-ups, redirects, or unusual behavior suggesting malware
description: The computer is showing unexpected pop-up advertisements, the web browser redirects to unfamiliar websites, or unfamiliar programs and toolbars have appeared that the user never installed.
symptoms: Frequent pop-up advertisements, even when the browser is closed
Browser homepage or search engine changed without permission
Unfamiliar toolbars or browser extensions appear
Computer runs unusually slow or the fan runs constantly
Antivirus software is disabled or missing without the user turning it off
Unknown programs appear in the installed programs list
possible_causes: Malware installed accidentally through a suspicious download or email attachment
A bundled unwanted program installed alongside legitimate software
Browser hijacker changing search and homepage settings
Adware displaying unwanted advertisements
Compromised browser extension
Outdated antivirus software failing to catch new threats
diagnostic_questions: When did you first notice this behavior?
Did you recently download and install any new software, especially free programs?
Did you click on any suspicious email links or attachments recently?
Is your antivirus software active and up to date?
Are the pop-ups appearing inside the browser, or even when the browser is closed?

commands.purpose: Check for unfamiliar startup programs that may be part of a malware infection
commands.expected_result: Only recognized, trusted programs appear in the startup list
commands.abnormal_result: Unfamiliar or oddly named programs appear, which may indicate malware

commands.purpose: Check for unusual network connections that could indicate malware communicating with a remote server
commands.expected_result: Connections match known, trusted programs
commands.abnormal_result: Unusual connections to unfamiliar addresses from unknown processes

troubleshooting_steps.action: Disconnect the computer from the internet temporarily if malware is confirmed or suspected to be actively spreading or stealing data
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This stops the malware from communicating with its source or spreading further while it is being removed

troubleshooting_steps.action: Run a full scan using the computer's installed antivirus software
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This is the first and most direct way to detect and remove common malware

troubleshooting_steps.action: If the built-in antivirus does not find anything but symptoms continue, run a scan using a dedicated malware removal tool
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Different security tools can catch different types of threats that others may miss

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check the list of installed programs for anything unfamiliar and uninstall unwanted programs
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Many unwanted programs, like adware, are technically installed as normal software and can be removed the same way

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check the web browser's extensions and remove any that are unfamiliar or were not intentionally installed
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Malicious browser extensions are a common source of pop-ups and redirects

troubleshooting_steps.action: Reset the browser's homepage and search engine settings back to a trusted default
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This removes changes made by browser hijacker malware

troubleshooting_steps.action: Change important passwords, such as email and banking, from a different, clean device after the malware is removed
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Some malware steals saved passwords, so changing them limits damage after an infection

troubleshooting_steps.action: If symptoms continue after cleaning, consider a full reinstall of Windows as the most reliable option
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Some malware hides very deeply in the system and can only be fully guaranteed removed with a fresh installation

possible_solutions: Run a full antivirus scan and remove detected threats
Use a dedicated malware removal tool for deeper scanning
Uninstall unwanted or unfamiliar programs
Remove suspicious browser extensions and reset browser settings
Change important account passwords after cleaning
Reinstall Windows if the infection cannot be fully removed
prevention: Only download software from official, trusted websites
Keep antivirus software active and updated
Be cautious with email attachments and links from unknown senders
Read installation screens carefully to avoid bundled unwanted software
Keep Windows and browsers updated with the latest security patches

problem: Computer shows warnings about disk errors or the disk is making unusual noises
description: The computer displays a warning message about a possible hard drive failure, or the user notices unusual clicking, grinding, or beeping noises coming from inside the computer.
symptoms: Warning message such as 'S.M.A.R.T. failure predicted' or 'disk error'
Unusual clicking or grinding noise from the computer
Files disappear or become corrupted unexpectedly
Computer freezes often, especially when opening or saving files
Very slow file access, or the computer takes a long time to boot
possible_causes: The hard drive is physically failing due to age or wear
The drive has bad sectors developing on its surface
Sudden power loss or physical shock damaged the drive
Cable or connection problem giving false failure signs
Overheating affecting drive reliability
Manufacturing defect in the drive
diagnostic_questions: Did you hear any unusual noises, like clicking or grinding, coming from the computer?
Has the computer experienced any recent power loss or been dropped or bumped?
How old is the computer or the hard drive?
Are you able to back up important files right now?
Did the warning message give any error code or drive name?

commands.purpose: Quickly check the basic health status reported by each disk drive
commands.expected_result: Status shows 'OK' for each listed drive
commands.abnormal_result: Status shows anything other than OK, such as 'Pred Fail', indicating a drive is failing

commands.purpose: Scan the drive for file system errors and bad sectors, and attempt repairs
commands.expected_result: Scan completes with no errors found
commands.abnormal_result: Bad sectors found and marked, or the scan cannot complete, indicating serious drive damage

troubleshooting_steps.action: Back up all important files immediately to another drive, cloud storage, or USB drive
troubleshooting_steps.reason: If the drive is truly failing, data can be lost at any time, so backing up right away is the most urgent priority
